docs.title: Lexikanon
docs.text:
Korean and English tokenizers, text normalizers, and stopword lists. Lexikanon is a plain Python library; it also ships HyFI 2.0 config groups, so the same tokenizers can be selected and run from HyFI workflows.

  • Documentation
  • Migrating from 0.x

Lexikanon 1.0 drops the HyFI 1.x API. Pin lexikanon<1 to keep it.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add lexikanon          # or: pip install lexikanon
pip install 'lexikanon[datasets]'     # tokenize_dataset / extract_tokens on datasets.Dataset
pip install 'lexikanon[similarity]'   # find_similar_docs_by_clustering

Python 3.11 or newer. Korean morphological analysis uses MeCab through eKoNLPy (fugashi and mecab-ko-dic wheels). On Python 3.15, fugashi builds from source and needs the MeCab library (apt-get install libmecab-dev or brew install mecab).

docs.title: Use it as a library
docs.text:
from lexikanon.normalizers import Normalizer
from lexikanon.tokenizers import MecabTokenizer

tokenizer = MecabTokenizer(noun_postags=["NNG", "NNP"])
tokenizer("금통위는 물가안정과 금리정책을 밝혔다.")
# ['금통위/NNG', '는/JX', '물가/NNG', '안정/NNG', '과/JC', ...]
tokenizer.nouns("금통위는 물가안정과 금리정책을 밝혔다.")

Normalizer(hanja2hangle=True)("今年에도 持續하고 있다")
# '금년에도 지속하고 있다'

Importing lexikanon never imports HyFI.

docs.title: Use it from HyFI
docs.text:
Installing lexikanon registers its config groups through the hyfi.plugins entry point:

group options tokenizer default, simple, mecab, nltk, nltk_universal normalizer default, formal_ko, informal_ko, formal_en, formal_en_parantheses stopwords default workflow lexikanon_tokenize_text, lexikanon_tokenize_dataset, lexikanon_find_similar_docs 
hyfi plugins
hyfi run workflow=lexikanon_tokenize_text tokenizer=mecab

import hyfi

tokenizer = hyfi.instantiate(hyfi.compose_group("tokenizer", "mecab"))

See Usage for workflow steps and presets.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Tokenize texts and datasets.Dataset columns; each function works as a HyFI workflow step.

In a workflow, pass the tokenizer as a config with _target_ (or ${tokenizer} from the tokenizer group); HyFI builds it before calling the step.

docs.title: Normalizer
docs.text:
Bases: Model

Main Normalizer class for generic text. Normalize unicode, hyphens, quotes, whitespace. By default, the normal form NFKC is used for unicode normalization. This applies a compatibility decomposition, under which equivalent characters are unified, followed by a canonical composition. See Python docs for information on normal forms: http://docs.python.org/2/library/unicodedata.html#unicodedata.normalize

docs.title: Stopwords
docs.text:
Bases: Model

A word is a stopword when stopwords_fn returns True for it or it is in the loaded list.

The set operators combine that rule, not just the lists: a | b and a + b match a word either operand matches, a & b one both match, a - b one a matches and b does not, and a ^ b one exactly one operand matches. The result keeps the operands' lowercase; operands that differ in lowercase raise ValueError, and so does & when both have a stopwords_fn (the result would have no finite list).

name: stopwords lowercase: true stopwords_fn: stopwords_list: stopwords_path: nltk_stopwords_lang: verbose: False

docs.title: Migrating from 0.x
docs.text:
Lexikanon 1.0 runs on HyFI 2.0 and no longer imports HyFI itself. To stay on the old API, pin lexikanon<1 (which needs hyfi<2 and Python below 3.13).

0.x 1.0 from lexikanon import HyFI import hyfi (HyFI 2.0), only where you compose configs HyFI.compose_as_dict("tokenizer=mecab") + MecabTokenizer(**cfg) hyfi.instantiate(hyfi.compose_group("tokenizer", "mecab")) HyFI.instantiate_config("stopwords", overrides=[...]) hyfi.instantiate(hyfi.compose_group("stopwords", "default", [...])) option __init__ (stopwords=__init__, /normalizer@normalizer: __init__) option default Normalizer() composed normalizer/__init__.yaml on construction Normalizer() uses class defaults, which now match that file (hanja2hangle=False) NLTKTagger.generate_config() and other HyFI model helpers removed lexikanon console command (hyfi_main wrapper) the hyfi CLI run=tokenize_dataset, pipe=extract_tokens, ... workflow=lexikanon_tokenize_dataset, workflow=lexikanon_find_similar_docs tokenize_dataset(data, tokenizer="mecab") (a config name) tokenize_dataset(data, tokenizer=MecabTokenizer(...)), or ${tokenizer} in a workflow about group removed

Outputs did not change: the tests compare every tokenizer and normalizer preset against results recorded with lexikanon 0.6.5 (tests/data/outputs_1x.json).

Fixed along the way:

  • The NLTK tagger downloads punkt_tab and averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng, which nltk 3.9+ needs; 0.6.5 failed on a clean machine.
  • find_similar_docs_by_clustering works on scikit-learn 1.4+ (metric= instead of affinity=), with the default distance_threshold=None, and with ids that are not row positions.

docs.title: stopwords_fn no longer evaluates strings
docs.text:
0.x passed a string such as "lambda w: len(w) < 2" to eval, so any config could run arbitrary code, outside HyFI's execution allowlist. 1.0 rejects strings. Pass a callable from Python, or in a HyFI config point at a function and allow it:

stopwords_fn:
  _target_: mypkg.text.is_short
  _partial_: true

hyfi run workflow=... --allow 'lexikanon.*' --allow mypkg.text.is_short

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
Every class is a Pydantic model; construct it with keyword arguments.

class module what it does Tokenizer, SimpleTokenizer lexikanon.tokenizers whitespace tokens MecabTokenizer (+ MecabTagger) lexikanon.tokenizers Korean morphemes as term/POS, via eKoNLPy NLTKTokenizer (+ NLTKTagger) lexikanon.tokenizers English tokens with Penn or universal tags, Porter stemming by default Normalizer lexikanon.normalizers ftfy, quotes, hyphens, whitespace, optional hanja to hangul and emoticon folding Stopwords lexikanon.stopwords a word list from a file, a list, NLTK, or a function

A tokenizer holds a normalizer and stopwords. tokenize() normalizes and tags; nouns() and tokens() filter by noun_postags, postags, and stop_postags, then drop stopwords.

Class defaults are minimal: MecabTokenizer() has no POS filters, so nouns() keeps every token. The presets below (tokenizer=mecab and so on) carry the POS lists; copy them from src/lexikanon/conf/ or compose them with HyFI.

The NLTK tagger downloads punkt_tab, averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng, universal_tagset, wordnet, and omw-1.4 on construction. Set NLTK_DATA to choose where they go.

docs.title: Config groups
docs.text:
option what changes from default tokenizer=simple SimpleTokenizer, strip_pos: true tokenizer=mecab MecabTokenizer, Sejong POS lists for nouns, punctuation, and stop tags tokenizer=nltk NLTKTokenizer, Penn POS lists, normalizer=formal_en tokenizer=nltk_universal nltk with the universal tagset normalizer=formal_ko hanja2hangle: true normalizer=informal_ko formal_ko plus emoticon folding normalizer=formal_en ftfy.unescape_html: auto normalizer=formal_en_parantheses all brackets become ( and )

Every node has a _target_, so hyfi.instantiate builds the object:

import hyfi

tok = hyfi.instantiate(hyfi.compose_group("tokenizer", "mecab", ["tokenizer.strip_pos=true"]))

docs.title: Workflow steps
docs.text:
The functions in lexikanon.pipes take their data as the first argument, so they chain as HyFI workflow steps:

  • lexikanon.pipes.tokenize.tokenize_texts(texts, tokenizer=None): a string or list of strings to lists of tokens.
  • lexikanon.pipes.tokenize.tokenize_dataset(data, tokenizer=None, text_col="text", token_col="tokens", ...): adds a token column to a datasets.Dataset (extra datasets).
  • lexikanon.pipes.tokenize.extract_tokens(data, tokenizer=None, token_col="tokens", extracted_col="extracted_tokens", nouns_only=False, ...): filters a token column by POS and stopwords.
  • lexikanon.pipes.similarity.find_similar_docs_by_clustering(data, ...): flags near-duplicate documents per time window in a pandas DataFrame (extra similarity).

tokenizer=None means SimpleTokenizer(strip_pos=True), the same as tokenizer=simple. In a workflow, pass ${tokenizer}; the example workflows pull tokenizer: simple into the root of the config, so tokenizer=<option> on the command line swaps it:

# conf/workflow/my_corpus.yaml
defaults:
  - /tokenizer@_global_.tokenizer: mecab

name: my_corpus
steps:
  - run: datasets.load_dataset
    with: {path: csv, data_files: data/news.csv, split: train}
  - run: lexikanon.pipes.tokenize.tokenize_dataset
    with: {tokenizer: "${tokenizer}", text_col: body}
  - run: lexikanon.pipes.tokenize.extract_tokens
    with: {tokenizer: "${tokenizer}", nouns_only: true}

hyfi run workflow=my_corpus --allow 'lexikanon.*' --allow 'datasets.*' --allow 'nltk.*'

The NLTK presets build nltk.stem.* objects, so allow nltk.* when you pass --allow.
